message:
Please review the following document.

<document>
Budget Justification: Extended Opening Hours at Five Branch Libraries, 2027-28
Library Services, Westmoor Borough Council, September 2026

1. Request
Library Services requests a growth bid of £174,000 in the 2027-28 revenue budget to extend opening hours at five branch libraries (Ashgrove, Fenwick, Holt Lane, Kingsmead and Millbrook) by ten hours a week each, from 38 to 48 hours.

2. Rationale
The five branches currently close at 5 pm on weekdays and do not open on Sundays. Residents' surveys have repeatedly identified opening hours as the main barrier to library use among working-age adults: in the 2025 Residents' Survey, 44% of non-users aged 25-54 said the library "is never open when I can go". The Council Plan commits to increasing library use among working-age residents and to supporting adult learning and job-seeking.

Each branch would add late opening until 8 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays (six additional hours) and Sunday opening from 11 am to 3 pm (four additional hours).

3. Evidence from the Ashgrove pilot
From October 2025 to March 2026, Ashgrove trialled exactly this pattern, funded from one-off underspends.

Table 1. Ashgrove pilot: average visits per opening hour, October 2025 to March 2026
Time slot | Visits per hour
Weekday 9 am - 12 pm | 46
Weekday 12 pm - 5 pm | 58
Tuesday and Thursday 5 pm - 8 pm (new) | 21
Saturday 9 am - 1 pm | 64
Sunday 11 am - 3 pm (new) | 52

Over the pilot, Ashgrove recorded 1,140 new library memberships, compared with 690 in the same months a year earlier. Sunday sessions were particularly popular with families, and a weekly job club in the Thursday evening slot was fully booked from its third week.

Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level, which shows that there is strong latent demand for evening opening and that the new hours will be well used across all five branches.

4. Costs
Additional hours need two staff on duty at all times, in line with the Council's lone-working policy. Staffing is calculated on 50 weeks a year, allowing for bank holiday closures.

Table 2. Cost of extended hours, five branches
Item | Basis | Cost
Staffing | 10 hours x 2 staff x 50 weeks x 5 branches = 5,000 hours at £24.80 per hour (including on-costs) | £124,000
Utilities and caretaking | £6,500 per branch | £32,500
Self-service kiosk upgrades (maintenance contract) | 5 branches | £7,500
Total | | £174,000

The staffing rate is the mid-point of the Library Assistant grade plus 28% on-costs and an enhancement for Sunday working. Utilities and caretaking costs are based on the actual additional costs recorded at Ashgrove during the pilot, scaled to a full year.

5. Value for money
At current visit rates, the extra hours across the five branches would generate roughly 84,000 additional visits a year, at a cost of around £2 per visit. This compares favourably with the borough's average cost per library visit of £3.40.

6. Alternatives considered
We considered opening the branches with self-service access only in the extra hours, as some authorities have done. This would cut staffing costs by around two-thirds, but the Council's insurers have advised that unstaffed opening would require building alterations and CCTV at an estimated £60,000 per branch, and it would not support the job club and family activities that drove much of the pilot's success.

7. Risks
Recruitment. We expect to fill most additional hours from existing part-time staff who have asked for more hours, as happened during the pilot.
Demand at other branches. Ashgrove is our busiest branch, and demand at the other four may be lower. We will review usage after six months.

8. Conclusion
The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand for evening and Sunday opening, with new memberships up by two-thirds and evening use close to daytime levels. We ask Members to approve a growth bid of £174,000 to extend this successful model to all five branches from April 2027.
</document>
response:
# Review: Extended Opening Hours Budget Justification

The case is clear and well organised, and most of the arithmetic holds up. But there are three factual errors that Members or Finance will likely spot, and the central evidence argument overstates what the pilot shows. All of these should be fixed before submission.

## Errors to correct

**1. The cost table doesn't add up.**
£124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = **£164,000**, not £174,000. Either the total is wrong or a £10,000 line is missing. Because the £174,000 figure appears in Sections 1 and 8, check which is correct and update all three places.

**2. The evening usage claim contradicts Table 1.**
Section 3 says evening visits "averaged close to the weekday daytime level." The table shows 21 visits per hour in the evening against 46–58 in the daytime. That is less than half. The conclusion repeats the claim ("evening use close to daytime levels"). This is the most serious problem, because a reader who checks the table will doubt the rest of the paper.

**3. The pilot lasted six months, not twelve.**
October 2025 to March 2026 is six months. The conclusion's "twelve-month Ashgrove pilot" is wrong.

## Weaknesses in the argument

**Evening opening is the weak part of the case, and the paper should say so.** The data actually tells a more nuanced and still useful story:

| Slot | Visits/hr | Staff cost per visit (2 × £24.80 ÷ visits) |
|---|---|---|
| Sunday | 52 | ~£0.95 |
| Tue/Thu evening | 21 | ~£2.36 |

Sunday opening performs nearly as well as Saturday. Evenings are much weaker, though the job club suggests they meet a real need. It would be more credible to present it this way. You could also note that the pilot ran through the darkest months, which may have depressed evening use.

**The extrapolation to all five branches is undermined by the paper itself.** The 84,000-visit estimate is arithmetically right (334 extra visits/week × 50 weeks × 5 branches ≈ 83,500). However, it assumes every branch matches Ashgrove, and Section 7 admits Ashgrove is the busiest branch. Consider:
- presenting a range, for example scaling by each branch's current visits per hour relative to Ashgrove;
- or describing 84,000 as an upper estimate.

**The value-for-money comparison isn't like-for-like.** The £2 per visit figure is a marginal cost: staffing, utilities and kiosks only. The £3.40 borough average presumably includes stock, buildings, management and overheads. Comparing them flatters the proposal. Either compare against a marginal figure or add a caveat.

**"Additional" visits may partly be displaced visits.** Some evening and Sunday users may simply have shifted from other times. Did weekday or Saturday visits at Ashgrove fall during the pilot? If not, say so, because that strengthens the case.

**The membership increase isn't clearly linked to the new hours.** Memberships rose by 65% (1,140 vs 690). Was this driven by the new slots, or partly by other factors such as promotion around the pilot? If sign-ups by time slot are available, include them.

## Costing points to clarify

- **Kiosks:** The line says "upgrades" but the basis says "maintenance contract." Is this one-off or recurring, capital or revenue? Also explain why kiosks are needed if the extra hours are fully staffed.
- **Utilities:** These are scaled from an October–March pilot. Winter heating and lighting costs will overstate a full-year figure, and Ashgrove's building may not be typical of the other four.
- **Staffing rate:** This is a single blended rate including a Sunday enhancement. State the assumed Sunday premium, and say whether any evening enhancement applies, so Finance can check it.

## Alternatives and risks

- **Missing options.** The paper considers only "all 10 hours staffed" versus "self-service." Members will likely ask about:
  - Sunday-only opening (4 hours, the strongest slot), at roughly 40% of the cost;
  - one late evening instead of two, perhaps Thursday to keep the job club;
  - re-profiling existing hours, for example shifting some of the quieter weekday mornings (46/hr) into evenings or Sundays at little or no extra cost.
- **Self-service comparison.** £60,000 × 5 = £300,000 one-off, against staffing savings of roughly £83,000 a year (two-thirds of £124,000). That is a payback of under four years. The non-financial reasons for rejecting it are reasonable, but show the numbers.
- **Recruitment risk is understated.** The pilot needed about 20 extra staff hours a week at one branch. The full scheme needs about 100 a week across five branches. Say how many existing staff have asked for more hours.
- **The six-month review has no criteria.** Set a threshold, such as a minimum visits per hour, below which a branch's extended hours would be cut back. This makes the bid easier to approve.

## Summary

| Priority | Issue |
|---|---|
| Must fix | Total (£164k vs £174k); "evening close to daytime" claim; "twelve-month" pilot |
| Should fix | Extrapolation from busiest branch; marginal vs average cost comparison; kiosk line |
| Would strengthen | Cheaper options (Sunday-only, one evening, re-profiling); recruitment numbers; review criteria |

I'd suggest reframing the case around the strong Sunday result and the specific value of evening activities like the job club, rather than claiming evenings match daytime use.
